# LLM surface list — athenaeum#1731
#
# One path per line, relative to the repo root. Blank lines and lines
# starting with `#` are ignored. An entry ending in `/` matches any path
# under that directory (prefix match); anything else must match a changed
# path exactly.
#
# This is the ONE file both `scripts/check_llm_surface_receipt.py` (the
# `.github/workflows/eval-receipt-check.yml` gate) and
# `tests/test_llm_surface.py` (the rot check) read — see that test's
# docstring for what "rot" means here.
#
# Two provenances, both legitimate:
#
#   MACHINE-ENFORCED — `tests/test_llm_surface.py` fails CI if either of
#   these sets gains a member not listed below:
#     - every `src/athenaeum/*.py` file that imports `LLMBackend`
#       (`grep -l LLMBackend src/athenaeum/*.py`, the athenaeum#1731 AC1
#       oracle)
#     - every module registered in `src/athenaeum/prompt_registry.py`'s
#       `PROMPT_META` (i.e. every module that owns a prompt indexed in
#       `PROMPTS`)
#
#   HAND-CURATED — from the athenaeum#1731 architecture survey (2026-09-16),
#   not derived by any test, but no less real a surface: the model-knob
#   resolution seam and the sidecar delivery path. Nothing removes these
#   automatically, so an intentional removal (e.g. `config.py` losing its
#   model-knob functions) should drop the entry in the same PR.
#
# The rot check is a SUBSET check (machine-enforced sets subset-of this
# file), not equality — hand-curated entries are always legal even though
# no test requires them.
